title: A recognized transient upstream error is now LABELLED on the artifact-timeout cause but still costs the full silence budget — short-circuit the wait instead of spending 600s to learn what the pane said in second 3
summary: Residual of transient-api-error-invisible-inside-artifact-timeout (delivered 2026-08-21, PR #478, main 5c0a9822). That fix added a driver-authored transient=true|false field to the ONE artifact-timeout marker line, matched from a per-family manifest transient_regex against the agent-stripped pane, and deliberately stopped there: the exit code was untouched so eval transient-bridge-retry AC-1 stayed green by construction. The consequence is that cycles 1523/1524/1526's actual cost is UNCHANGED — the router still burns waited=600s interval=300s extends_used=1 before dying, and for the router the CLI fallback chain (agy -> claude) is already consumed by then, so degrade-to-static-spine remains the only move. cycle-1526 pays it twice per cycle (initial plan + post-scout re-plan). The signal now exists in-process at the moment of detection; nothing consumes it.
root_cause: ADR-0090 chose disclosure-as-data over reclassification, for a good reason (see its Alternatives table): making exit 81 retryable regresses transient-bridge-retry AC-1, which correctly pins that a generic artifact timeout means 'agent stalled, investigate' — blind retry of a real wedge costs a second full budget. But the ADR only closed the DIAGNOSIS gap. The pane is scanned once, at teardown (driver_tmux_repl.go, just before `return ExitArtifactTimeout`), i.e. AFTER the budget is already spent. The same classifier could run on the per-tick pane the wait loop already captures (`curPane`, the same place the exhaustion detector runs at driver_tmux_repl.go:767 via livenessCenter.ExhaustedOf) — where a match is actionable in seconds rather than post-mortem.
fix: Do NOT make exit 81 retryable (AC-1). Instead move/duplicate the recognition to the WAIT LOOP so a recognized transient error can end the wait early with a DISTINCT, already-retryable disposition rather than a generic exit 81. Two candidate shapes, both needing design review before code: (A) a distinct exit code that isTransientBridgeError already admits (80/85/86/124) or a NEW one added to the sentinel — exit 81's contract is then untouched because this death never IS an 81; (B) keep exit 81 but have the driver stop extending once transient is recognized and persistent, so the death arrives at ~1 interval instead of 1+max_extends. Shape (A) is preferred: it makes the disposition explicit and lets the orchestrator's existing transient retry/backoff path handle it, rather than teaching the timeout path a second meaning. CRITICAL constraint carried over from the cycle-1528 premise-challenge: the classifier must read the PANE, never the stderr buffer Engine.Launch inspects. ALSO carry over the persistence discipline the exhaustion detector already uses (exhaustion_persistence.go): a single transient-looking frame must NOT fast-fail a working agent — the wall detector learned this the hard way, and a 529 that self-recovers on the provider's side is exactly the case that would otherwise kill a healthy phase. Reuse that gate rather than inventing a second one.

acceptance: A pane carrying a recognized transient upstream error, persisting across the persistence gate's threshold, ends the artifact wait in ~1 review interval instead of interval*(1+max_extends) — asserted on wall-clock/extends_used, not merely on a label.
The resulting death classifies as retryable through the EXISTING isTransientBridgeError path (no new bespoke retry logic).

eval transient-bridge-retry AC-1 stays green: a generic exit 81 with no recognized transient error is still NOT transient. Run internal/core TestIsTransientBridgeError + TestIsTransientBridgeError_StaysTransientOnly.
A SINGLE transient-looking frame that clears on the next tick does NOT end the wait (persistence gate honored) — a working agent is never killed by one bad frame.
A pane matching exhausted_regex still escalates as a wall, not as a transient retry (no path collision, both directions).
Family-agnostic: driven for at least one NON-claude family, mirroring TestRunTmuxREPL_ArtifactTimeout_TransientFieldIsFamilyAgnostic.

notes: Filed by the console session that landed PR #478, so the deferred half is queued rather than lost to session memory. Evidence base: .evolve/runs/cycle-{1523,1524,1526}/router-escalation-report.json (final_pane carries the verbatim 529 text); a live fixture is already checked in at go/internal/bridge/testdata/cycle-1523-router-529-pane.txt. SECOND, SEPARABLE RESIDUAL also open: only claude-tmux's transient_regex is grounded in a live captured pane — codex/agy/ollama patterns come from those providers' documented error shapes and have never been validated against a real pane (a log sweep found 6 'Overloaded' hits, all Claude). Recognition is fail-open, so a miss costs only the label, but the FIRST non-claude occurrence recorded with transient=false on a pane that plainly shows a server error is the evidence to correct that family's regex. Worth a cheap grep over .evolve/runs/*/router-escalation-report.json after any batch that dispatched a non-claude family. || 2026-08-22 DESIGN REVIEW: BLOCK on the originally-preferred shape (A). Two claims verified hands-on in the console before accepting: defaultFallbackOnExit lacks any new code (llmroute.go:57), and the tracked cycle-1523 fixture matches claude's own transient_regex. The approved ReviewStop variant needs no new exit code and preserves every #478 diagnostic. NOT implemented this session — it is 7 changes in the hottest bridge path and lands at SHADOW, so it would produce no wave signal anyway. Design is now pre-baked for whoever picks it up.

design_review.verdict: BLOCK on shape (A) as specified; PROCEED on the ReviewStop variant below
design_review.reviewer: architect (opus), console design review — the review this item itself demanded before code
why_blocked: DECISIVE: a new exit code 82 is NOT in llmroute.defaultFallbackOnExit{80,81,85,124,127} (llmroute.go:57, VERIFIED). Plan.TriggersFallback would be false, so Dispatch/DispatchTiered stop at the first candidate. Shape (A) would ship a 4s death with NO CLI fallback — strictly worse than today's 600s death, which DOES fail over.

Reusing an existing code is disqualified: 85 drives the tier step-down (llmroute/tier_fallback.go:14,89) and the all-families DEFERRED checkpoint (core/quota_exhaustion.go:25-35) — a 529 relabelled 85 would demote the phase a model tier then abort the loop; 80 records a boot strike and benches the family (engine.go:579-583); 86 carries loop-guard semantics; 124 is the gnu timeout(1) convention and overloading it makes forensics unanswerable.

SELF-KILL HAZARD (VERIFIED): the TRACKED fixture go/internal/bridge/testdata/cycle-1523-router-529-pane.txt:32 matches claude's OWN transient_regex ('API Error: 529'). docs/architecture/full-tmux-control.md:300 and ADR-0090:32 carry the same string. Any cycle whose scope is this very item renders the text on-pane and gets killed in 4s on every candidate in its chain, on both attempts.

The proposed per-family trust key (transient_shortcircuit) therefore protects the WRONG families: it would enable claude — the one family exposed in this repo — and gate the three whose regexes are merely unvalidated. It is also dispatch policy living in a vocabulary file (breaks ADR-0090 decisions 4-5) and violates no_feature_flags_use_design_patterns; it cannot be soaked or disabled mid-incident.

The persistence gate is NOT the missing guard. wallcorroborate.go:6-11 (the 2026-08-15 false-wall post-mortem) states that prompt-echo strip + persistence gate are STRUCTURALLY DEFEATED by a lane whose work content is the vocabulary — which is why the exhaustion path needed a third out-of-band guard (wallCorroborated) before it was allowed to kill.

Porting exhaustionGate's 2-observation threshold from the 300s checkpoint to the 2s fast-poll keeps the mechanism's reputation for safety while discarding 99.3% of its evidence (600s -> 4s). agy/codex carry bootScrollback=200 (driver_agytmux.go:39) vs claude's 0, so a recovered 529 stays matchable for 25 minutes there — the gate is inverted, not merely weak.

DIAGNOSABILITY: returning an rc from the switch (driver_tmux_repl.go:709-726, like case 85) skips the entire `if !completed` block at :878-942 — deleting the artifact-timeout marker line PR #478 just built, writeEscalationReport, warnExhaustionRegexDrift, the workspace listing, AND engine.go:557's cause lift (scoped to code==ExitArtifactTimeout). It would be a new phase-kill path LESS diagnosable than the timeout it replaces.

RETRY WINDOW: PhaseMaxAttempts=2, RetryBackoffBaseS=5 (policy.go:1024-1026). Today the 600s wait IS the de-facto recovery delay. Removing it lands both attempts inside the same upstream weather window ~15s apart, converting 'slow but eventually succeeds' into 'fast and fails'.
approved_design: 1. DROP the new exit code. Trigger the EXISTING ReviewStop mechanism (stopreview.go:73, fatalpane.go:107-113): it breaks at driver_tmux_repl.go:872 INTO the !completed block, so the escalation report, the #478 marker line (incl. transient=true), the cause lift and exit 81 are all preserved. AC-1 untouched (still 81), fallback chain untouched (81 IS a trigger), backfill still eligible, ADR-0090 decision 1 preserved verbatim — an amendment, not a supersession. Zero rows in the exit-code wiring table.

2. Cache the pattern at construction in newAutoResponder (autorespond.go:319-327), pre-compiled, mirroring exhaustedRegex. classifyTransientPane currently does LoadManifest -> os.ReadFile + unmarshal + overlayManifestCatalog (package mutex) + fresh regex compile PER CALL — ~900 of those per phase on a 2s poll.

3. TIME-BASED DWELL, not observation count: record firstSeenAt, reset on any non-match, fire only after a configured dwell (start 60s = 90% budget saving with 30x the evidence of a 2-frame port). Do NOT reuse exhaustionGate unmodified — its threshold was calibrated for a 300s cadence.

4. Gate on NON-BUSY (copy fatalpane.go:84's ev.Busy guard). The cycle-1523 pane had already gone idle ('Sauteed for 3m 28s', nudge at the prompt) — idleness is the real discriminator, and stopreview's prime directive (never kill a working agent) outranks the saving.

5. STAGE the action via the existing ADR-0044 dial (fatalpane.go:19-29: off|shadow|enforce, default shadow, policy-resolved via Deps.RecoveryStage + channel.ResolveStage) with interaction.Recorder outcomes would_fast_fail/fast_failed, so the false-positive rate is MEASURED on real panes before the flip. This subsumes the per-family concern with one operator-controllable knob.

6. If per-family discipline is still wanted, encode the EVIDENCE not the PERMISSION: a manifest transient_regex_evidence pin (e.g. 'cycle-1523-router-529-pane.txt') that the enforcement site requires. Keeps the manifest descriptive and makes ADR-0090's 'evidence asymmetry, stated' section machine-checkable.

7. Answer the rc-discarding callers explicitly (driver_tmux_repl.go:309 boot loop, capture_models.go:80, recipe_adapter.go:98,136,221 — three of four discard rc): scope the dwell tracker to the wait loop or latch like wallProbed/wallConfirmed.
8. Add a deliberate re-dispatch delay so attempt 2 does not land in the same weather window.

9. Correct docs/architecture/full-tmux-control.md:308 only if the exit code ever changes — under the approved design it does not, so no correction is needed and the section 7a transient=true playbook stays live.
design_review.shape_b_note: Shape (B) (stop extending) is safe but buys only ~300s, not ~594s: the incident line waited=600 interval=300 extends_used=1 means max_extends was effectively 1. The ReviewStop variant dominates it for barely more work.
